Conditions raised by zurds

Source: R/conditions.R
zurds-conditions.Rd

Every error zurds raises carries a condition class, so it can be caught by kind rather than by matching the message, which may change. Every class below inherits from zurds_error.

Details

zurds_invalid_argument

An argument was unusable. Carries arg, the argument at fault.

zurds_format_error

The input is not a file R wrote: bad magic, an unknown format character or an unsupported version.

zurds_parse_error

The stream is malformed. Carries offset, the byte offset in the decompressed stream, and path, where in the object the walk was.

zurds_unsafe_content

The file holds something the data-only reader refuses. Carries findings, as rds_scan() would report them.

zurds_not_found

A name or path is not in the file.

zurds_encoding_error

A string is not valid in its declared encoding.

zurds_limit_error

A limit was reached. The subclasses zurds_depth_limit, zurds_size_limit and zurds_item_limit name which one. Carries limit, the argument's name, and limit_value.

zurds_io_error

Reading the input failed.

zurds_decompression_error

The input could not be decompressed, for example because it is truncated.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "promise.rds", package = "zurds")
cnd <- tryCatch(rds_read_data(f), zurds_unsafe_content = function(e) e)
class(cnd)
#> [1] "zurds_unsafe_content" "zurds_error"          "error"               
#> [4] "condition"           
cnd$findings
#>    path finding detail severity
#> 1 [[2]] promise   <NA> executes

tryCatch(rds_info(charToRaw("not R")), zurds_format_error = conditionMessage)
#> [1] "not an R serialization stream: unknown magic bytes"
